requirements.heading: Purpose
requirements.text: Please note that while the parent "multipart/report" content type defined in [REPORT] is used for all kinds of administrative messages, this format is intended specifically for communications among providers regarding email abuse and related issues, and SHOULD NOT be used for other reports.

requirements.heading: Format of Email Feedback Reports
requirements.text: The first MIME part of the message contains a human-readable description of the report and MUST be included.

requirements.heading: Format of Email Feedback Reports
requirements.text: The second MIME part of the message is a machine-readable section with the content type of "message/feedback-report" (defined later in this memo) and MUST be included.

requirements.heading: Format of Email Feedback Reports
requirements.text: This part MUST be included (contrary to [REPORT]).

requirements.heading: Format of Email Feedback Reports
requirements.text: While some operators may choose to modify or redact this portion for privacy or legal reasons, it is RECOMMENDED that the entire original email message be included without any modification as such modifications can impede forensic work by the recipient of this report.

requirements.heading: Format of Email Feedback Reports
requirements.text: Except as discussed below, each feedback report MUST be related to only a single email message.

requirements.heading: Format of Email Feedback Reports
requirements.text: The Subject header field of the feedback report SHOULD be the same as the included email message about which the report is being generated.

requirements.heading: Format of Email Feedback Reports
requirements.text: If it differs, the difference MUST be limited to only a typical forwarding prefix used by Mail User Agents (MUAs) such as "FW:".

requirements.heading: Format of Email Feedback Reports
requirements.text: The second part contains additional derived data that may help the receiver, but in terms of selecting actionable report data, report recipients SHOULD use the content of the third part first, then data from the second part.

requirements.heading: Format of Email Feedback Reports
requirements.text: The first part is meant to contain explanatory text for human use but is not itself a part of the report, and SHOULD NOT be used if it is in conflict with the other parts.

requirements.heading: The 'message/feedback-report' Content Type
requirements.text: Although these fields have a syntax similar to those of mail message header fields, they are semantically distinct; hence, they SHOULD NOT be repeated as header fields of the message containing the report.

requirements.heading: The 'message/feedback-report' Content Type

requirements.text: The following report header fields MUST appear exactly once:

requirements.heading: Required Fields
requirements.text: The format of this field MUST follow section 14.43 of [HTTP].

requirements.heading: Required Fields
requirements.text: This field is for documentation only; there is no registry of user agent names or versions, and report receivers SHOULD NOT expect user agent names to belong to a known set.

requirements.heading: Optional Fields Appearing Once
requirements.text: The following header fields are optional and MUST NOT appear more than once:

requirements.heading: Optional Fields Appearing Once
requirements.text: This field MUST be formatted as per section 3.3 of [MAIL].

requirements.heading: Optional Fields Appearing Once
requirements.text: Addresses MUST be formatted as per section 4.1.3 of [SMTP].

requirements.heading: Optional Fields Appearing Once
requirements.text: The historic field "Received-Date" SHOULD also be accepted and interpreted identically to "Arrival-Date".

requirements.heading: Optional Fields Appearing Once
requirements.text: However, if both are present, the report is malformed and SHOULD be treated as described in Section 4.

requirements.heading: Optional Fields Appearing Multiple Times
requirements.text: This field SHOULD be repeated for every SMTP recipient seen by the report generator.

requirements.heading: Handling Malformed Reports
requirements.text: When an agent that accepts and handles ARF messages receives a message that purports (by MIME type) to be an ARF message but syntactically deviates from this specification, that agent SHOULD ignore or reject the message.

requirements.heading: Handling Malformed Reports
requirements.text: Where rejection is performed, the rejection notice (either via an [SMTP] reply or generation of a [DSN]) SHOULD identify the specific cause for the rejection.

requirements.heading: Extensibility
requirements.text: In order to encourage extensibility and interoperability of this format, implementors MUST ignore any fields or report types they do not explicitly support.

requirements.heading: Extensibility
requirements.text: Such types and fields MUST be registered as described above and published in an Open Specification such as an RFC.

requirements.heading: Extensibility
requirements.text: Experimental report types and report header fields MUST only be used between ADMDs that have explicitly consented to use them.

requirements.heading: MIME Type Registration of 'message/feedback-report'
requirements.text: Encoding considerations: "7bit" encoding is sufficient and MUST be used to maintain readability when viewed by non-MIME mail readers.

requirements.heading: MIME Type Registration of 'message/feedback-report'
requirements.text: Interoperability considerations: Implementors MUST ignore any fields they do not support.

requirements.heading: Feedback Report Header Fields
requirements.text: New registrations or updates MUST be published in accordance with the "Specification Required" guidelines as described in [IANA].

requirements.heading: Interpretation
requirements.text: The authentication and validity of the content of the report SHOULD be established through other means.

requirements.heading: Intentionally Malformed Reports
requirements.text: Implementors SHOULD thoroughly verify all such messages and be robust against intentionally as well as unintentionally malformed messages.

requirements.heading: Attached Malware
requirements.text: As this format is sometimes used to automatically report malware, ARF processors (human or otherwise) SHOULD ensure that attachments are processed in a manner appropriate for unverified and potentially hostile data.

requirements.heading: The User-Agent Field
requirements.text: It is intended for documentation and debugging, and since it is trivially forged by a malicious agent, it SHOULD NOT be interpreted by recipients.
